_note: One short paragraph per test module for Section 6.3.4 (what the module's test cases verify), written from the test names and bodies in tests/test_*.py. The counts in front of it (cases, passed, failed) are generated from the recorded run. Re-read when tests are added.
Sign-in, access control, API errors and: Sign-in was verified to lock an account after repeated failures even for the right password, to give every failure the same generic answer, to take the role from the server and not from the login form, to clear the session on sign-out and refuse a replayed cookie, and to keep login responses out of any cache. Demonstration mode was verified to default on, to hide every demonstration endpoint and leak no password when switched off, and to list demonstration accounts only when on; a generated password was verified to be changed before anything else. Every API route was verified to refuse an anonymous client, every route declared for other roles to refuse an account of a different role, and a student to see, change or delete only the student's own record, files, submissions and messages. Malformed requests and unknown routes were verified to return JSON errors, and start-up tasks to be idempotent, to be skipped under a test runner, and not to reset a password a faculty member chose.
Monitoring sheet, import and data integr: The import was verified to take the standing from the note column with provenance, to leave the stage and standing of an existing non-active student alone, to give imported accounts random passwords outside demonstration mode, and to keep flags typed and audited so that a corrected workbook resolves them, including for several students at once. Portal entry was verified: staff can create a student with the same validations as the import, add and edit subject rows with provenance and an audit trail, change an imported value only with a reason, delete softly with a reason, add the remaining curriculum subjects in bulk, and keep a free-form row out of the curriculum count. A later import was verified to keep a portal edit and raise an issue for staff, write access to be limited to the entitled roles, and portal-entered students and rows to flow into the workbook export, enrollment, reports and the student portal. Merging two duplicate students was verified to move every linked table and leave no login orphaned.
Enrollment, course offering and course a: Course offering setup and class-list import were verified end to end, including that a class-list file must match the selected term, that a date outside the term is an error, that the Dean-approved faculty member is never overwritten, and that publishing never deletes an offering that has enrolled students. The enrollment guard was verified to name every blocking standing, to stop a subject being active in two semesters, to flag an overload from the register, and to require resolution for a subject that is not offered. The subject-needs report and demand were verified to count everyone who still needs a subject, to list the full delay impact even for one student, and to use authoritative curricula. The plan cycle was verified: the Dean must comment when returning a plan, a draft cannot reset an approved plan, and approval hands the plan to the role that can publish. The admission onboarding report, the coursework report, curriculum tagging, study plans, academic semesters and the disabling of grade writes were also verified.
Research gate, panel matching and defens: Panel matching was verified to rank by recorded expertise so that different papers give different panels, to give every candidate an explainable breakdown, to drop the student's own adviser, to follow the panel composition and size rules of the Research Protocol by paper type and stage, to label its method honestly and fall back from Gemini to TF-IDF, to fail closed when calendar availability is unavailable, and to require the endorsed Form 1 first. Faculty calendar authorization was verified to be limited to the faculty member's own account. Scheduling was verified: the lead time is counted from the Form 1 endorsement or from the day the panel received the manuscript, a slot in the past is never allowed, an override needs a recorded reason, a second booking for the same stage must go through reschedule, cancellation and rescheduling need a reason and keep the old record, and a panel change puts the schedule on hold until availability is rechecked. Verdicts were verified: title outcomes are approved or disapproved, a score below the threshold cannot be a plain pass, minor revisions complete the stage only after the adviser confirms, a provisional pass with re-defense reopens scheduling, a deferred defense is rebooked and linked, and the chair can correct a verdict with a reason until the student has acted on it. Ethics was verified to be recorded only after a passed defense.
Practicum: The completion path and the incomplete-certificate loop were both verified, including the addition of a further certificate without replacing the submission history. Practicum was verified to be restricted to the Psychology and MSGC programs, and student submission was verified to be locked until the eligibility conditions are met. Existing demonstration students were verified to migrate to the configured programs, and practicum tasks were verified to close through the real flow.
Graduation: The return, resubmit, approve, and export sequence was verified end to end. Application was verified to require eligibility together with the signed document, and incomplete coursework and incomplete research were verified to route to staff rather than fail silently. Batch processing was verified to skip unverified candidates while sending those that are eligible, and completion evidence uploads were verified to feed the graduation checklist. Confirmed revisions were verified to count as a passed defense for graduation, and the policy assistant was verified to forecast next-semester graduation readiness.
Leave of absence and readmission: Leave and readmission requests were verified to be rows of one case table with their own fields, to move only between known statuses, each move needing the right status and the right role and being written to the case history with who and why, and a second request while one is open to be refused with a helpful message. The rules were verified: two semesters a request and four in total, a single extension right after the leave, no leave in the last two weeks of a semester, the policy check using the date the request was filed, and years in program counting leave. Side effects were verified: an approved leave that starts later is scheduled and begins on its first day, a leave in the running semester closes its subjects at once, a leave filed in the second half of the semester marks subjects W, a leave can be cancelled or revoked before it starts, and a leave that is ending becomes return due, after which AWOL is proposed and staff confirm it. Readmission was verified to apply only to a student on leave and to restore the stage and close the leave. The Registrar list was verified to be case based with handoff states and an export log, and never to include a request that was not approved. Batch forwarding and batch decisions, the student notices, the work queue tasks and the demonstration students' stories were also verified.
AWOL and residency: A return from AWOL was verified to be policy-reviewed and decided by the Dean, and the absolute residence limit was verified to require re-enrollment with a valid residency record. Every residency figure was verified to come from one function, and the residency watchlist to flag students past their limit. Students on leave or AWOL were verified to be refused by student self-enrollment and by the class-list import.
Subject withdrawal and dropping: The approval sequence and the denial branch were both verified, as was the rule that a student may submit within the withdrawal window and that a late request is blocked. Marking a subject dropped was verified to be restricted to the Academic Coordinator, with an effective date inside the semester, and to close a pending withdrawal request for that subject. An approved subject withdrawal was verified to leave the student's standing untouched, a student to be able to file another withdrawal after an export, and withdrawal tasks to close as each step completes. A subject dropped in the same term was verified not to be silently re-enrolled, including by the class-list import.
Policy assistant and policy documents: The assistant was verified to reject staff-only questions asked by a student, to keep a student in the student's own sandbox, to give short cited answers from the uploaded library, to fall back to local retrieval when the document search fails or no key is set, to route paraphrased requests for operational figures to the verified reports, and to prefer semantic vectors while keeping the lexical fallback. The document library was verified: staff can upload PDF and Word documents with category, effective date and status, replace a file while the previous version stays on disk and in history, and delete every version; only the current version is indexed; a draft is searchable but every answer says it is pending validation; an archived document is not searched; scanned PDFs are read by optical character recognition where available, with readable errors otherwise; and damaged or hostile files get a readable error. Library management was verified to be limited to staff and the administrator, and every signed-in role to be able to ask a policy question.
Business rules register: The register was verified to be seeded without ever overwriting an edited value, to name the source of every rule and to explain why a rule is not enforced, to be readable by any signed-in user and changeable only by staff and the administrator with a reason that writes a revision and an activity-log entry. The rules were verified to drive the workflows: the withdrawal window and its fee tiers, the drop rule and its absence limit, the add and change windows, the full-time load, the leave period, total and filing date, maximum residence that never pauses for leave, the defense lead days and panel sizes, the practicum requirements and faculty load, and the comprehensive examination gate. The product was verified to carry no leftover penalty-free or seven-day wording.
Operations manual content: The operations manual draft was verified for internal consistency: rule identifiers are unique, prefixed by chapter and consecutive, every rule has a valid status, official rules cite a page or section, Handbook citations use printed page numbers, practice rules name a consultation or notes, every chapter has the same parts, references to rules and open questions exist, and the generated rules file matches the content.
Portals, dashboard, reports and work que: The dashboard, the students list, the stage chart, the standing filters and the work queue were verified to give the same totals, the at-risk and on-leave states to have one meaning everywhere, report counts to be real with only the rows paged, and decision-support totals not to be cut by the page limit. An overdue task was verified to move a student to at risk without a restart, queue aging not to count finished cases, and the Research Coordinator's work queue to need only readable data. The analytics reports were verified to generate, the nine KPI measurements to be computed and to fall when a report fails or a role gate drifts, and completion and attrition to be computed per program. Deep links were verified to serve the single-page application without swallowing API routes.
Workflow tasks, messages, audit and data: A clarification was verified to be returned and answered, request files to be scoped to the student and the workflow role, and the student inbox to hide internal messages and track read state. A reviewer transition was verified to create a linked student notice and an audit entry. Tasks were verified to close only for the acting office, a message not to finish the sender's task, and start-up cleanup to close the tasks of workflows that already finished. Owner labels were verified to have one spelling, legacy rows to be migrated safely and repeatably, every screen to count the same staff tasks, and long log text to be cut to the column size. Students were verified not to receive faculty contact details, and no database file to be tracked by the repository.
Adviser appointment, calendars and notif: Availability was verified to be whatever the faculty member enters: nothing is entered by default, no busy blocks are invented, entering weekly hours stamps the update, a dated entry replaces that day's hours, unavailable dates and part-days are cut out, and only the owner can delete an entry. Staff were verified to be able to ask for availability without duplicate open requests, and slot checks to separate hard conflicts (a time in the past, outside entered hours, a double-booked panel member, the same room) from soft warnings (before the lead time, availability not entered). The adviser appointment was verified end to end in the protocol order by the right role, including that only the nominated adviser can respond, that one application is open at a time, that a decline or a Dean refusal lets the student nominate again, that the limit of five advisees blocks an appointment unless the Dean records an exception, that contract forms become overdue after five days, and that a change of adviser needs a reason and both advisers to agree, is allowed only once and not after the proposal defense. Existing advisers were verified to be migrated safely and only once. The calendars were verified to show each role only what it should, to flag a finished defense without a verdict, and to add the protocol deadlines. Panel invitations were verified to appear for every seat, to need a reason for a decline, and to raise a reschedule request when a member cannot attend. Notifications were verified to start empty, to be created for bookings, reschedules, cancellations and adviser steps, to produce reminders at 14, 7, 2 and 1 days only once, and to count as read when opened. The private calendar link was verified to work without a session, to hold only that person's calendar, to be replaced or revoked on request, and to give nothing for an unknown token or a disabled account.
